title: Data classification & segregation schedule — embedded model integrations (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft defines a schedule of data classification decisions and segregation requirements for integrations that embed or serve models (embeddings, chat, rerankers, KV caches) — both for Redwood-hosted and Private deployments. Goal is to provide consistent, auditable rules vendors/integrations must meet and a checklist for engineering/security reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to upstream model requests/responses, generated embeddings, cached KV layers, telemetry derived from requests (e.g., latency-traces with token previews), and any persisted prompt sets used for eval/monitoring.
- Covers Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) variants where Redwood software or partner code processes customer data.
- Does NOT replace legal DPA but provides operational mappings and controls referenced in contracts.

Quick summary (decision highlights):
- Classified data tiers: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, SENSITIVE, RESTRICTED.
- Embeddings and model outputs default to SENSITIVE unless explicitly labeled PUBLIC by the customer.
- KV cache + prefix caches are considered RESTRICTED if they can be material for customer PII/significant IP.
- Tenant-level cryptographic isolation required for RESTRICTED; envelope encryption with customer KMS encouraged for Private.

Definitions and classification rules:
- PUBLIC: information intended for public distribution (marketing copy, public docs). No special retention or encryption required beyond platform baseline.
- INTERNAL: non-public internal notes, service metadata, non-sensitive telemetry. Retention short (30–90 days) unless otherwise noted.
- SENSITIVE: customer PII, non-public product roadmaps, model prompts tied to customer identity, embeddings derived from private docs. Typical retention window 90–365 days; encryption at rest and in transit required.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (health/financial), legal secrets, or caches that could be used to reconstruct private data (large persisted KV caches, embeddings for high-similarity private corpora). Requires tenant cryptographic separation and stricter access controls, minimal retention, and audit evidence.

Model-specific considerations:
- Embeddings: treat as SENSITIVE by default. If embeddings are used for vector search against customer corpus that contains RESTRICTED data, vector store and snapshot artifacts must be treated as RESTRICTED.
- Chat Responses: the generated output is SENSITIVE if the prompt contains SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED content. Should not be stored by default; if stored (for evaluation/QA), mark classification and follow retention.
- KV/Prefix Caches: even transient caches may hold sensitive spans. For multi-tenant hosts, cache keys and storage must be namespaced and encrypted. Persistent caches that contain customer-derived KV entries are RESTRICTED.
- Telemetry and Traces: token-sampled traces are SENSITIVE; strip or redact tokens by default. High-fidelity traces that include PII require explicit customer opt-in and are logged as RESTRICTED.

Technical controls by classification (mapping schedule):
- PUBLIC: baseline platform TLS, standard RBAC. Retention default: 365+ days (unless customer requests shorter).
- INTERNAL: TLS, at-rest encryption with platform keys, role-based access limited to engineers. Retention default: 90 days.
- SENSITIVE: TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at-rest; separate database schemas per tenant recommended. Access logs retained 1 year. Redaction and tokenization applied where feasible. Retention default: 90–365 days.
- RESTRICTED: Customer-specific KMS (BYOK) strongly recommended. Envelope encryption, HSM-backed KMS for Private. Tenant-dedicated storage (logical or physical). Access requires 2-person approval for retrieval, detailed audit trail, and quarterly attestation. Retention default: minimal (30–90 days) unless contract requires otherwise.

Operational checklist for integrations (to be completed during security review):
- Data mapping: list all data items sent to model endpoints, their classification, and storage paths. (Linked template: CONFLUENCE PIA table)
- Storage review: verify whether embeddings, caches, or logs are persisted; if yes, identify classification and encryption scheme.
- Tenant isolation: confirm namespace, RBAC, and whether the integration supports tenant-specific keys.
- Retention policy: set default retention per classification and ensure deletion workflows for backups/snapshots.
- Access controls: list service accounts with access; enforce least privilege and rotate keys quarterly.
- Auditing: enable request/response ID correlation and immutable logs for RESTRICTED data; provide sample retention export for auditors.
- Data flow diagram: include annotated flow with classification labels for each hop (ingest, cache, storage, telemetry).

Vendor / third-party supplier requirements (when Redwood integrates external vector stores or middleware):
- Minimum security attestation: support for tenant namespaces, AES-256, role-based access, and API keys that can be rotated.
- Data residency: supplier must commit to the same residency constraints as customer contract.
- Deletion guarantees: supplier must expose APIs that allow verified deletion and return deletion proofs.
- Penetration testing evidence and SOC2 or equivalent desired.

Sample schedule (text-table):
- Embedding snapshots: Classification = SENSITIVE; Default retention = 180 days; Encryption = platform AES-256; Isolation = logical tenant schema.
- Live KV caches (ephemeral < 1h): Classification = INTERNAL; Default retention = 0 (evicted); Encryption = in-memory TLS only.
- Persistent KV store ( > 24h): Classification = RESTRICTED if contains customer confidential; Default retention = 30-90 days; Encryption = envelope with customer KMS for Private.

Open questions / decisions needed (notes to reviewers):
- Do we enforce BYOK for all RESTRICTED customers or only on request? Recommendation: require BYOK for enterprise contracts that specify RESTRICTED data in DPA.
- How granular should token redaction be for telemetry traces? (tradeoffs in debugging vs. privacy)
- Define exact audit format we will provide to auditors for deletion proofs.

Implementation notes for engineering teams:
- Config flags: integrations should expose a classification label on each request (public|internal|sensitive|restricted). Runtime must map label to storage/retention behavior.
- Backwards compat: default unlabeled requests should be treated as SENSITIVE to avoid accidental exposure.
- Migration: rolling migration plan for existing embeddings stores — inventory, tag by tenant/class, migrate to encrypted buckets during next maintenance window.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence PIA: CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD://privacy/pia-embedded-models
- Vendor assessment template: shared_drives/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-assessment-questionnaire-template-v1.json
- DPA clauses: shared_drives/security-and-compliance/data-processing-schedule-and-security-attachment-saas-integration.json
- Implementation PR TODO: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/678

Decision log (history):
- 2024-09-18: Draft created (Ava Patel).
- 2024-09-22: Engineering feedback: prefer SENSITIVE default for unlabeled inputs (not PUBLIC).
- 2024-10-01: Legal requested clearer retention brackets for RESTRICTED.

Action items before finalization:
- [ ] Security to confirm BYOK policy and update boilerplate contract language (owner: Marisol).
- [ ] Eng to provide sample deletion-proof API response (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Privacy to sign off on telemetry redaction guidance (owner: Diego).

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally operational — it is intended to be linked from DPAs and vendor exhibits as the behavior we will attest to. Please focus review on the RESTRICTED controls (KMS, audit, deletion proofs) and whether any controls should be escalated to contractual obligations.
